feature: Thickness in Appearance makes a drawn line thicker
summary: Raising Thickness on a line, an arrow or a Pen path now thickens it on the canvas, live, by dragging or typing, and one Command Z puts it back. Before, the number changed and the line stayed as thin as it was drawn.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: outline-width-walk (picture, slider clicks) and line-thickness-typed-walk (typed numbers, the next line, a video).

try.do: Before the fix: draw a line with the Line tool, pick it, click the Thickness track. The panel says 26 and the line is still 4 pixels thick (counted on the render: 4px before, 4px after).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Now: draw a line, pick it, click or drag the Thickness track to 26. The line on the canvas is 26 pixels thick (measured on the render: 4px to 26px).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z once. The line is back to 4 pixels; Shift Command Z takes it to 26 again.
Click the Thickness number, type 12 and press Return. The line is drawn 12 pixels thick (measured 4px to 12px).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw another line with the Line tool. It starts at 12 (measured 12px).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw an arrow and a Pen path and raise their Thickness. The arrow shaft measures 40px at the top of the slider, the path 26px.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: On a new video (File, New Video), draw a line, type 30 into Thickness. The line on the canvas measures 30px.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does a line you thicken now look the way you expected the first time you tried it?
Does the next line starting at the width you just chose feel right, or should each line start at the stock 4?
At the top of the slider, does the arrowhead look big enough for the shaft, or should the head grow more with the line?
rough: No mock covers this: the fix changes what the canvas draws, not the panel, which is unchanged.

At 40 the arrowhead is only a little wider than its shaft (the head grows at 0.6 of the line width). That is the existing head sizing, with Head Size beside it to grow it; written in this task log rather than filed.

On a 1400x900 video window with the line picked, Appearance is squeezed to a sliver above the Library pane, so Thickness is off screen (last picture). Folded into on-a-video-captions-and-transitions-sit-where-th, which owns that panel layout.
The new pixel check a walk uses (expectInk) has not yet been watched on a locked screen; it renders the document the way the render step does, so it is listed as lock safe by reading.
